items.headline: Loonie sinks to 18-month low as jobs shock kills BoC hike bets
bullets: Numbers: USD/CAD 1.4275 (-0.4% Friday); touched 1.4298 intraday — weakest since April 2025; fifth straight weekly loss.
Meaning: the -68.3K jobs print keeps biting — Oct 28 hike odds down to 25% from 40%; Canada 2Y -6.8bp to 3.183%, ~161bp below the US 2Y (widest since Feb 2025).
FX read-through: market now prices BoC on hold at best — any CAD rally fights a widening rate gap. Oil softer (WTI $91.19) isn't helping.

bullets: Numbers: -68,300 jobs in September (consensus +9,200); unemployment 6.5% (from 6.4%); second straight monthly loss after -41,700 in August; 2026 YTD now -41,200; participation 64.8%, lowest in 29 years outside the pandemic; wages +2.3% y/y.

Meaning: losses led by public sector (education + healthcare -58,400), not tariffs — but this was the last jobs print before the Oct 28 BoC decision, and it kills the creeping December-hike pricing. Canada 2Y fell 8bp to ~3.20%.

FX read-through: USD/CAD up to ~1.4275 (from ~1.4225), near 52-week highs — the market is trading the miss. CAD's oil tailwind now fights a weak domestic story; the ~160bp US-Canada 2Y gap is the anchor.
Next: Canada CPI Oct 21, then BoC decision Oct 28.
